sentences: From the hairline, down the nose to the upper lip, a single green stripe divides the woman's face in two.
The sitter is the artist's wife, Amélie Matisse, and one side of her face is painted in pink and orange, the other in yellow, turning light and shadow into planes of colour.
The background splits the same way, pink and orange on one side and teal on the other.

In the summer of 1905 Matisse worked with André Derain in the fishing village of Collioure, experimenting with freeing colour from its descriptive job, and this portrait was most likely painted that autumn after his return to Paris.
Around this time a critic called these painters 'les fauves', the wild beasts, and the name Fauvism was born.
Reactions were mixed: a friend of the painting's owners, Michael and Sarah Stein, called it 'a demented caricature of a portrait'.
Now regarded as a masterpiece of twentieth-century portraiture, it was reproduced in a book on Matisse in 1920 and entered the National Gallery of Denmark in 1936.
